metadata.title: Global Novel Virus Incidence: A Regional Analysis
metadata.description: Quarterly reported cases of a new viral strain across different geographical areas, illustrating variations in prevalence and regional health strategies.
metadata.main_insight: Daily new COVID-19 cases peaked and subsequently decreased in the EU, U.S., India, and Russia between 2020 and early 2021. The timing and magnitude of the peaks varied among the regions.

datafacts.annotation: The Ratio of U.S. and India show a positive correlation.
datafacts.reason: The Pearson correlation coefficient of the Ratio between U.S. and India is {r:.2f}, indicating a strong positive relationship.

datafacts.annotation: The U.S. shows a sudden jump in Ratio from Mid 2020 to Late 2020.
datafacts.reason: The Ratio for U.S. increases from 75000.0 at Mid 2020 to 200000.0 at Late 2020, indicating a sharp change.

datafacts.annotation: The Russia shows a sudden jump in Ratio from Early 2020 to Mid 2020.
datafacts.reason: The Ratio for Russia increases from 5000.0 at Early 2020 to 20000.0 at Mid 2020, indicating a sharp change.

datafacts.annotation: The total value of EU, U.S. all have the largest proportion.
datafacts.reason: The total value of Ratio of EU, U.S. all account for 0.375, larger than all other Region, of the total of Ratio of all Region.

datafacts.annotation: The EU, U.S. all have the largest proportion in Late 2020.
